stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer, llama, and AI/ML community.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: Google and Epic give up fighting — third-party Android app stores are coming next week
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Google and Epic Games have dropped their legal battle regarding Android app store policies.
The resolution forces Google to allow and carry third-party app stores within the Google Play ecosystem.
This marks a significant shift in the Android app distribution landscape in the US.

stories.title: Microsoft’s Secure Boot has been broken for a decade and no one noticed until now
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Microsoft's Secure Boot feature has a known vulnerability dating back a decade.
The vulnerability stems from unrevoked, old 'shims' within the system.
This flaw allows for relatively simple bypasses of the security mechanism.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
Relevant technologies include transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when running with coding agents, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its 'local-first' capability, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with the popular local LLM runner.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, now integrates MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing occurs on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Lawsuit claims Meta's layoff decisions were made by AI, not humans
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A lawsuit alleges that Meta utilized Artificial Intelligence in its workforce layoff decisions.
The legal challenge specifically claims AI was involved in terminating employees with disabilities or medical issues.
Meta has publicly denied the accusation, stating that AI was not used in these termination processes.

stories.title: New York bans data center construction for a year, rattling AI industry
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: New York has implemented a one-year moratorium on new data center construction.
This regulatory action is being viewed as a potential model for broader anti-AI sentiment.
The ban directly impacts the infrastructure requirements of the rapidly expanding AI industry.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often lack the ability to estimate task complexity, leading to inefficient execution.
The research proposes 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' as a missing capability for agents.
This capability aims to guide agents toward the shortest, most efficient path rather than defaulting to maximum-context processing.

stories.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
stories.author: Wei Zhan
bullet_points: Introduces TerraZero, a new procedural driving simulator and self-play training stack for autonomous vehicles.
Addresses key challenges in AV training: the need for speed, real-world map realism, and diversity to cover safety-critical edge cases.
Achieves high performance by running simulation on the CPU and policy inference on the GPU via a zero-copy path, sustaining 1.3M agent-steps.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed for running native LLM agents directly on mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current agent systems, which are typically server-based, by enabling on-device execution.
Highlights the importance of mobile devices as key agent environments due to their accessibility and access to user data/sensors.

stories.title: Audio-Native Speech Recognition with a Frozen Discrete-Diffusion Language Model
stories.author: Vineet Agarwal
bullet_points: Proposes an alternative to traditional autoregressive decoders for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) using a discrete diffusion language model.
The method refines the entire transcript in parallel over a few denoising steps, contrasting with token-by-token generation.
The system utilizes an audio-native interface trained on DiffusionGemma, a 26B MoE model, employing a uniform, random-token discrete diffusion process.

stories.title: Resist and Update: Counterfactual Report Coordinates for Incentive-Compatible LLMs
stories.author: Yuen-Hei Yeung
bullet_points: Addresses a critical failure in aligned LLMs: misreporting under non-evidential incentive pressure (e.g., agreeing with a confident user).
Proposes a novel method using 'counterfactual report mediators' to enforce internal incentive-compatibility (IC).
The proposed mediators ensure model reports are invariant to forbidden influences (like pressure) while remaining responsive to genuine evidence.

stories.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
stories.author: Wei Zhan
bullet_points: Introduces TerraZero, a procedural driving simulator and self-play training stack for autonomous vehicles.
Addresses key challenges in AV training: speed (1.3M agent-steps/sec), realism, and coverage of rare, safety-critical scenarios.
Features a high-performance architecture utilizing a CPU-based simulation engine and GPU-based policy inference via zero-copy path.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed for running LLM agents natively on mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current agent systems being primarily desktop/server-based, which restricts mobile accessibility.
Highlights the importance of mobile devices as key agent environments due to their ubiquity and access to user data/sensors.

stories.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips under Task-Irrelevant Context
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: State-of-the-art LLMs appear robust to task-irrelevant context when measured by aggregate accuracy.
This aggregate stability is misleading, as it masks significant per-example prediction instability.
The research highlights a critical vulnerability in LLM deployment in context-rich environments.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's existing MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the context and knowledge base of Claude Code.

stories.title: Samsung’s new foldable display is harder to crease and damage
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Samsung introduced 'Flex Titanium,' a new flexible display technology for foldable phones.
The new tech aims to make foldable displays slimmer, more durable, and reduce creasing.
The improvement is expected to debut with the upcoming Galaxy Z Fold 8.

stories.title: Microsoft’s biggest ever patch Tuesday lets you hold off updating for longer
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Microsoft released a major Patch Tuesday update for Windows 11.
The update addresses a large number of security vulnerabilities, reportedly fixing at least 570 holes.
Users are now given the option to pause Windows updates indefinitely.

stories.title: US military sent explosive drone boats into combat for the first time
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The US military deployed explosive drone boats for combat operations.
The attack targeted an Iranian naval port.
The action is occurring amid escalating tensions between the US and Iran.

stories.title: These painted e-tattoos could be the future of wearable biosensors
stories.author: Jennifer Ouellette
bullet_points: The article discusses the potential of painted e-tattoos as future wearable biosensors.
These sensors utilize conductive ink applied directly onto the skin.
The ink dries to form functional electrodes for biological monitoring.

stories.title: Google revamps image search for its 25th anniversary with more images and more AI
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is updating its image search functionality for its 25th anniversary.
The revamped search will leverage user's 'unique interests' to generate a personalized, always-updated gallery.
The update incorporates more AI capabilities into the image search experience.

stories.title: FormalAnalyticGeo: A Neural-Symbolic Based Framework for Multimodal Analytic Geometry Problem Generation
stories.author: Qiufeng Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FormalAnalyticGeo, a new neural-symbolic framework for generating multimodal analytic geometry problems.
Addresses the scarcity of annotated samples in analytic geometry, a domain less explored despite MLLM advancements.
Overcomes limitations of existing methods, such as template methods failing with constraints and generative models lacking geometric precision.

stories.title: Form, Not Content? A Preregistered, Placebo-Controlled Evaluation of Learned Error-Conditioned Self-Repair Through Prompts and Weights in Frozen Small Code Models
stories.author: Mehmet Iscan
bullet_points: Introduces PoPE (Popperian Placebo-controlled Evaluation), a new methodology to test LLM self-repair capabilities.
Addresses a gap in current self-repair literature by providing placebo controls for measuring error-conditioned learning in code LLMs.
Focuses on evaluating how well frozen, small, locally deployed code LLMs can use counterexamples (refutations) to correct their own code.

stories.title: The Seriality Gap in Video Diffusion Models
stories.author: Yutong Bai
bullet_points: Video diffusion models struggle with predicting long causal chains in dynamic systems (e.g., multi-ball collisions).
Performance degradation is linked to the dependent-event structure (interactions) rather than just the total video length.
The study isolates the issue by comparing multi-ball dynamics against single-ball control experiments.

stories.title: Watermark Forensics for Generative Models: An Information-Theoretic Perspective
stories.author: Jiankun Hu
bullet_points: The research proposes using watermarks in generative model outputs for advanced forensic analysis beyond simple machine-made detection.
These watermarks can be designed to attribute output to a specific user, extract hidden data payloads, or localize content surviving editing.
The study frames these capabilities as a 'forensic ladder,' analyzing the required sample length ($n$) for each level of forensic detail.

stories.title: Form, Not Content? A Preregistered, Placebo-Controlled Evaluation of Learned Error-Conditioned Self-Repair Through Prompts and Weights in Frozen Small Code Models
stories.author: Mehmet Iscan
bullet_points: Introduces PoPE (Popperian Placebo-controlled Evaluation), a new methodology for testing LLM self-repair.
Addresses a gap in self-repair literature by rigorously measuring how LLMs use error evidence (counterexamples) for correction.
Focuses on evaluating frozen, locally deployed small code LLMs using a controlled, falsification-based approach.

stories.title: LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes
stories.author: Henry Moss
bullet_points: Introduces LatentFlow, a general framework designed to condition stochastic processes.
Addresses the common difficulty in conditioning stochastic processes due to intractable conditional laws.
Key feature is that the framework requires no learned neural approximations or training.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often lack the ability to estimate task complexity, leading to inefficient execution.
The paper proposes 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' as a missing capability for LLM agents.
This capability aims to help agents determine the true difficulty and the most efficient path to complete a task.

stories.title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations
stories.author: Zhiyu Li
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'MemOps' to benchmark memory operations in long-horizon LLM conversations.
Current benchmarks are criticized for only testing final answer correctness, masking underlying memory failures.
MemOps aims to differentiate various memory failures, such as missing facts, incorrect binding, or stale data reliance.

stories.title: LLM Judges Can Be Too Generous When There Is No Reference Answer
stories.author: Sowmya Vajjala
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of using LLMs as judges for open-ended, no-reference NLP tasks.
It addresses the concern that LLM judges may be overly lenient or 'too generous' without a ground-truth answer.
The research employs a two-stage pipeline involving calibration and sensitivity experiments to test judge performance.

stories.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Misconceptions in Multi-Turn Medical Conversations
stories.author: Saiph Savage
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for LLMs to handle patient misconceptions in multi-turn medical conversations.
Highlights a gap in current evaluation frameworks regarding how LLMs manage evolving or persistent false beliefs.
Focuses on the complex requirement of not just answering, but actively identifying and correcting underlying patient misconceptions.

stories.title: Can LLMs Write Reliable Rubrics? A Meta-Evaluation for Experiment Reproduction
stories.author: Chenghua Lin
bullet_points: The paper addresses the scalability issue of rubric-based evaluation for LLM research agents, especially in paper reproduction tasks.
It presents the first systematic meta-evaluation of rubrics generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) for this purpose.
This research aims to reduce the substantial expert effort traditionally required to construct paper-specific evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: Knowledgeless Language Models: Suppressing Parametric Recall for Evidence-Grounded Language Modeling
stories.author: Jan Buys
bullet_points: Addresses the issue of LLMs relying too heavily on internal, potentially outdated 'parametric recall' for factual answers.
Proposes 'Knowledge-Less Language Models' (KLLMs) as a new training paradigm to shift LLMs toward evidence-grounded reasoning.
The research investigates modifying the pretraining signal to improve model reliability when context is provided.

stories.title: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques
stories.author: Jaegul Choo
bullet_points: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) offer theoretical advantages in parallel generation over standard autoregressive models.
Practical speedups in dLLMs require specialized inference mechanisms, such as diffusion-aware caching and reuse.
Recent research is heavily focused on exploring various acceleration techniques across algorithms and architectures to enable practical deployment.

stories.title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models
stories.author: Tapan Parikh
bullet_points: The study investigates answer-choice conformity among 44 different language models when forced to select a single word from many valid options.
A notable finding is that the word 'serendipity' was chosen by 41% of the models when prompted to 'pick a word -- any word.'
The research uses a minimal, controlled experimental setup (31 single-turn prompts) to characterize this convergence behavior without system prompts.

stories.title: I Put a Hailo 8 in a Handheld and Stopped Paying for Inference
stories.author: numbpill3d
bullet_points: The article discusses the shift from cloud-based AI inference to edge computing.
The author successfully deployed a Hailo 8 accelerator in a handheld device.
The core theme is reducing operational costs by moving AI processing locally instead of subscribing to cloud services.
